prompt: A $400$ mg dose of medicine loses HALF its amount every $4$ hours. After how many hours is only $25$ mg left?
hint: Count how many halvings take $400$ down to $25$, then convert halvings into hours.

hints.text: Count how many halvings take $400$ down to $25$, then convert halvings into hours.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $80$ mg down to $20$ mg is $2$ halvings ($80 \to 40 \to 20$). If each halving is $4$ hours, that is $8$ hours. Same move, more steps.

explanation: Halving means the decay factor is $\frac{1}{2}$.
Each halving takes $4$ hours, so $4 \times 4 = 16$ hours.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fill in a clock table
steps: Hour 0: $400$ mg. Hour 4: $200$ mg. Hour 8: $100$ mg.
The table lands on $25$ mg at hour $16$.
